title: This Beetle Can Survive Being Eaten Alive By A Toad
description:
This beetle carries two chemicals inside its body that explode when mixed -- and when a toad swallows it whole, that's exactly what it does, from the inside.

#shorts #sciencefacts #beetle #didyouknow
sources: Royal Society Biology Letters: Sugiura & Sato (2018), "Successful escape of bombardier beetles from predator digestive systems"
National Geographic's "See the Amazing Way a Beetle Survives Being Eaten"
Chemistry Steps' "The Chemistry Behind Bombardier Beetle's Spray"

scenes.text: There's a beetle that can survive actually being swallowed alive by a toad -- and it does it by setting off a chemical explosion inside the toad's own stomach.
It carries two separate chemicals inside its body that are harmless on their own. When threatened, it mixes them together on purpose, using its own internal enzymes as the trigger.
That reaction is genuinely explosive. It heats the mixture to the boiling point of water, and fires it out in rapid pulses -- up to five hundred tiny explosions every single second.
In a real 2018 study, researchers actually fed these beetles to toads on purpose, to see what would happen.
Once swallowed, the beetle sets off that same chemical explosion, this time inside the toad's stomach. The heat and irritation force the toad to vomit it back up, alive.
In that study, over ninety percent of the beetles survived being swallowed whole and blasted their way back out.
Would you have guessed a beetle could survive being eaten alive?
